from.place: proof step (2): every D(A) object is generated from shifts of A by direct sums, triangles, and retracts

title: Generation of a module derived category by shifts of the ring
statement: For a ring $A$, every object $K$ of $D(A)$ [def-pc-derived-category] belongs to the smallest full subcategory of $D(A)$ that contains all shifts $A[k]$, $k\in\mathbf Z$, and is closed under set-indexed direct sums, under the third vertex of a distinguished triangle whose other two vertices lie in it, and under retracts.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark 15.60.11 (more-algebra-remark-P-resolution), Tag 09PB, as invoked in perfect.tex Lemma 36.22.1 (Tag 08EU)
